B53-B58 numerically (p=0.5 gives F=0.4375, c=0.3906, F'=0.49 from both the p form and the F form), so c=(1+2F)^2/9 and F'=9F^2/(1+2F)^2 hold. Condition the value leaves implicit: depolarizing noise also on the ancillas, checks noiseless (Fig. 3). Note for the team lead: the derivation is a computation (a Mathematica contribution is named), not a theorem; graded high only on the shown derivation.
pcs-xz-qubit-cost: Section III.B.2, p.5: the paper's own count for its Fig. 5 scenario (4 ancillas, 6 physical qubits).
bbpssw-not-best-multiround: Section III.B.2, p.5: the paper states which benchmarks it uses (1, 2 and 3 round BBPSSW at 4, 8, 16 qubits) and that the concatenated protocol of [21], needing at least 8 qubits, is not compared. The value is attributive ('the authors state'). The 'not the best' remark rests on [21], and I grade only the scope of the benchmark.
recursive-pcs-design: Section III.B.3, p.5: the paper defines the recursion (checks whose targets are the previous ancillas; X checks only because Z errors on ancillas go undetected; two extra X checks per level). All in the same paragraph.
recursive-pcs-no-analytic-fidelity: Section III.B.3, p.5: the paper says it gives no analytic recursive fidelity, only numerical results in Fig. 11.
teleported-pcs-criteria: Section III.C, p.6 and Fig. 8 caption: the paper gives these as the postselection rule of its teleported PCS variant. Graded as the protocol's own rule; the derivation from stabilizers is not shown, so it is not a proved result.
sim-noise-setup: Section III.D, p.6: the paper's own simulation parameters (gate depolarization 0.001 and 0.01, channel rate 0 to 0.5).
sim-recursion-qubits: Section III.D (p.7) and Fig. 11 caption (p.9): the paper's qubit counts (6, 10, 14) for recursion 0, 1, 2.
pcs-future-work: Section IV, p.9: the paper names its own open line (further study of the recursive nature of PCS) and a hoped-for use of graph properties. Attributive value; graded as what the paper itself says it leaves open, not as a finding. The 'could prove to be useful' half is hope, not result.

theory_low.gong-shot-exponents-degree-independent: Appendix D.4, p.45 (rendered): the stated conservative bound is eps^-2 (Delta+1)^20 R^116 varsigma^-108 (N0/delta)^108, so its exponents are fixed numbers. But the paper does not show the algebra from Eqs. (20)-(22) to these exponents, and I could not reproduce 20 and 116 from kappa (Eq. 20) and eta (Eq. 22). A remark on constants, not a stated and proved result.
theory_low.gong-theorem2-informal-lattices: Theorem 2, p.7, is the informal form of Theorem 9. The value drops the smoothed-analysis condition, the probability 1-delta, and the size conditions of Theorem 9 (open chain length at least 4, periodic at least 9, rectangle sides at least 3, periodic at least 9), so it overstates for small lattices. LOW for dropped conditions; Theorem 9 itself (next item) is the graded statement.
theory_low.gong-derivative-estimation-cost: Appendix C.2, p.27: the quotes are the prose summary above Theorem 4 and drop its conditions (known local energy bound g, fixed locality m, chi and derivative order r, probability 1-delta'). Theorem 4/10 itself is proved in F.1 (Markov and Hoeffding inequalities, Chebyshev interpolation), but this value is the unconditioned summary. LOW for dropped conditions.
theory_low.hamlearn-computational-basis: The new value restores the letters (X and Z, from Section 2.2 'IXZ' definition, p.6) and adds the conditions: generic Gaussian-smoothed couplings and the nearest-neighbor truncation of the power-law tails (Section 2.2, p.6; Section 5, p.16). The reconstruction claim is proved (Theorems 7 and 9, with the caveats in the Theorem 9 item). But the value also carries 'a class which captures contemporary Rydberg atom platforms', an authors' relevance claim resting on cited platform Hamiltonians [22, 24, 33]. Graded by the weaker part, so LOW: a certainty change for the team lead. The reconstruction claim alone would be HIGH on proved result.; team lead, 2026-11-04, Sprint 15 Manual Validation Q1 option 1 (all 36 as proposed)
theory_low.gonon-monte-carlo-bound: Appendix C, p.15: the bound L1/sqrt(n) + 4R/sqrt(S) is shown (Minkowski plus Theorem II.4). The quote and the value drop its conditions: f in F_R, theta from Theorem II.4, i.i.d. shots, error in expectation. I decide LOW for the dropped conditions, not for the derivation.
theory_low.gonon-alt-circuit-2n-qubits: Remark II.3, p.3: a remark that the proof 'carries over analogously'. Remark VI.2 sketches it. The explicit circuit is left for future study. Not a proof of a stated result.
theory_low.gonon-no-curse-of-dimensionality: Remark II.6, p.4: this is the authors' interpretation, set against a result cited from [48] (O(eps^-d) basis functions). The n^(-1/2) rate in Theorem II.4 has no d in the exponent, but the constant L1[f] depends on f and can depend on d, which the paper does not discuss. Theorem IV.1's bound has an explicit sqrt(d) factor. A comparison and an interpretation, not a proved result.
theory_low.gonon-full-support-measure: Section II-C, p.5: a remark on Corollary II.7 with no proof of its own. It also reads the corollary loosely ('holds on all of Rd').
theory_low.gonon-larger-function-class: Section II-D, p.5: a comparison of Theorem II.4's class with Barron's condition, which is a cited result [9]-[11]. The authors' reading ('higher expressive power'), not a proved result of this paper.
theory_low.gonon-reservoir-eps-scaling: Section III opening, p.5: a restatement of Theorem III.4 as 'put differently' O(eps^-2) weights and O(log2(1/eps)) qubits. The quote drops the theorem's conditions (f in the compatible class, constants depend on f).
theory_low.gonon-remark-vi5-section2-analogue: Remark VI.5, p.11: a remark that the proof gives an analogue for the Section II circuit. The bound is only stated, not worked out.
theory_low.gonon-example-iii5-student-t: Example III.5, pp.6-7: an example. The H^1 reading follows from the t1 density, but the example drops that f must also be in C(R) and L1(R), and gives no derivation.
theory_low.gonon-corollary-iii6-mixture: Corollary III.6, p.7, proof in VI-D, p.11. The quotes and the value drop the conditions: s > d/2, nu = 2(s - d/2) tied to s, f in H^s and L1, constant C_{f,delta}. The 'arbitrarily close to any density' sentence is the authors' reading. LOW for the dropped conditions.
theory_low.gonon-conclusion-dimension-free: Section V, p.8: a summary sentence. It says 'all the derived bounds', but Theorem IV.1's bound carries an explicit sqrt(d) factor and the constants depend on f. An overgeneral summary, the authors' interpretation.
theory_low.gonon-appendix-b-generic-circuits: Appendix B, p.15: the argument is short and in the paper, but the value drops the conditions. 'Arbitrarily well' holds only in the mean-square sense under a probability measure mu, for a fixed theta-tilde, a measurable parametric gate and a diagonal observable. The quotes carry none of these. LOW for the dropped conditions.
theory_low.gonon-lemma-a2-psi-product: Lemma A.2, Appendix A, p.15 (I rendered the page). The lemma has a proof by induction, but its printed product runs i = 0 to n_l - 2, which counts n_l - 1 Hadamard qubits plus two |0> qubits, one more than n_l. The value states the intended reading (all but the last two qubits), not the printed formula. The paper's table agrees with the intended reading. LOW because value and printed lemma differ.
theory_low.pcs-single-check-improves: A statement that a single check improves fidelity 'as calculated in Appendix B'. Appendix B derives the one-ancilla fidelity F1' (Eq. B50) but never compares it with the unprotected fidelity or states the improvement. The authors' claim, not shown.
theory_low.pcs-xz-first-order: Stated expansion of Eq. (20); the paper gives no derivation. Unlike the X case, the X&Z formulas (17)-(20) have no appendix derivation.
theory_low.pcs-xz-vs-bbpssw-fidelity: A comparison of analytic curves read from Fig. 4b under one noise model (equal depolarization on all qubits); 'most of the domain' is a plot reading, not a proved bound. A measured/compared result, not a proof.
theory_low.pcs-xz-success-prob: Fig. 6 comparison of analytic curves under one noise model; 'slightly higher over most of the domain' is a plot reading. The comparison is the authors' result, not a proof.
theory_low.fig6-success-prob-crossover: From_figure value. I rendered p.6: PCS about 0.06 at F=0.25, BBPSSW about 0.12, crossing near 0.45. The reading is close, but a figure reading is never HIGH. The two quotes do not carry the numbers.
theory_low.recursive-pcs-polynomial-cost: The cost C(r)=4(r+1) is taken 'from Fig. 7' with no derivation; the polynomial claim is the authors' statement. It agrees with the Section III.D counts (6, 10, 14 qubits) but the paper does not argue it.
theory_low.pcs-xz-distance-1: Section III.B.4, p.5: the authors' statement about detection capability, no proof given in the paper.
theory_low.recursive-pcs-code-family: Section III.B.4, p.5: [[5,1,2]], [[7,1,2]] and the general [[2(r-1)+5,1,2]] family are stated; no derivation or stabilizer list is given in the paper.
theory_low.recursive-pcs-weight-bound: Section III.B.4, p.5: weight bound 4 stated; only the one weight-4 generator is shown, no proof of the bound for all r.
theory_low.recursive-pcs-css-equivalent: Section III.B.4, p.5: local equivalence to CSS codes stated with a pattern of H gates; no proof in the paper.
theory_low.recursive-pcs-tradeoff: Section III.B.4, p.5: the trade-off is argued from one worked example (the [[5,1,2]] circuit, syndrome [0010]); no general proof.
theory_low.pcs-beats-bbpssw-postselection: Conclusions, p.9: a comparison of analytic curves under one noise model, stated as a conclusion; the authors' claim, not a proof.
theory_low.pcs-outperforms-bbpssw-fidelity: The narrowed value adds the condition from the Fig. 4 captions (all qubits same depolarization) and matches the Conclusions sentence on p.9. It is a comparison of analytic curves under one noise model, an authors' result.

The first (a community-driven white paper that identifies and prioritizes R&D opportunities in hardware-based ML) is scope; the Abstract is on p.2 of the PDF, not p.1, and the same words are in Section 1. The second ('quantum computing remains in early stages for practical HEP deployment', Section 4.1.5 'Quantum Computing for HEP', p.93) is a field statement about the maturity of quantum computing, not a scope statement about this paper.
